text:
rachel: noticed a spike in 'duplicate ws messages' support tickets after the sticky-route ttl change. putting notes here while we triage.

jordi: what changed exactly?

rachel: we lowered sticky-lease TTL from 90s -> 20s in canary to reduce backend stickiness during failovers. After that, a few customers saw replays/duplicates during reconnects.

maya: do we have traces tying duplicates to route flips vs proxy buffering?

rachel: traced one tenant: client ws disconnected briefly, reconnected and landed on a different backend instance that had an out-of-date in-memory session registry. That backend replayed buffered events and also served resume from our global resume store, so client got overlapping streams (A,B then A again).

alex: so two sources of overlap: (1) backend with stale in-memory queue replaying and (2) global resume producing overlap. When combined they amplify duplicates.

jordi: is this only WebSocket or SSE too?

maya: mostly WS observed because some WS backends keep ephemeral per-conn ring buffers for low-latency retransmit. SSE backends tended to rely solely on resume id and didn't replay in-memory.

rachel: telemetry: console shows reconnect event and resume id, but no signal for "route-flip post-disconnect". support can't tell if client hit a new instance.

alex: we should add a per-connection tag: initial_backend_id + current_backend_id and emit a route_flip boolean on reconnect. That would make it trivial to query sessions that moved.

jordi: agree. Also recommend we add a backend-level metric: stale_session_replays++ when a backend serves from its in-memory buffer after a reconnect where resume_store was also used.

maya: quick mitigation: revert TTL change on canary pool until we have detection. But I think we can also implement a guard: when a backend accepts a resume request, it should consult the global resume store first and, if resume-store indicates overlap that would cause duplicate emission, backend should prefer resume-store output and suppress its local buffer replay.

alex: that's a good safety net. But need to be careful with performance: consulting global resume store adds an RPC. Could add a cheap local Bloom filter of recent resume ids to avoid RPCs in the common case.

jordi: for console/UX: show a new "route_flip" column on live session view and an explanation in the hover text about possible duplicates if local buffers exist. Also add an alert if >1% of reconnects in a minute had route_flip=true and emitted duplicates.

rachel: product impact: some customers rely on inclusive resume semantics; we must not change that behavior. The suppression should only dedupe internal replays (i.e., buffer-originated). Need clear telemetry to prove we didn't change client-visible guarantees.

maya: infra action items:
- Revert sticky-lease TTL change on canary pools (rachel will coordinate)
- Add route_flip telemetry tag on reconnects (jordi to PR)
- Backend: check resume-store before local-buffer-replay, add stale_session_replay metric (maya + sam)
- Console: add route flip column + an ad-hoc query to surface impacted tenants (alex + olivia)

infra-bot: Revert job scheduled: sticky-lease-ttl reset for canary pool at 2026-03-21T14:00:00Z.

jordi: I'll prototype the route_flip tag in the control plane; it's a small change to the reconnect RPC envelope (add prev_backend_id).

alex: timeline? we should be able to revert today, land route_flip metric within 24h, backend guard in 48-72h.

maya: I'll reach out to the tenant support rep and share a narrow repro. We should ask them to test against the reverted canary first.

rachel: agree. Also add a short blurb to release notes explaining why lowering TTL can surface duplicates for WS live-replay backends.

jordi: one more thought: for future rollouts, include a small ramp that asserts reconnect duplication rate doesn't spike beyond baseline before expanding. Add that to console rollout policy page.

alex: noted. I'll add rollout-gate checklist item.

maya: great. I'll drop logs & repro here once I have them. thanks all. :shipit:
